title: Finding the constant of proportionality
source: Theory P23-10.2 Quick check 1; dN/dt = kN with a given rate
stem: The rate of increase of a population \(N\) is proportional to \(N\). When \(N={N0|int}\), the population is increasing at a rate of \({r|int}\) per year. Writing \(\dfrac{dN}{dt}=kN\), find \(k\).

steps.name: K
steps.note: Substitute the given rate and value.

steps.name: A
steps.note: Solve for k.

contexts.note: Includes the original N = 400 increasing at 10 per year, k = 0.025

contexts.stem: The number of fish \(N\) in a lake grows at a rate proportional to \(N\). When there are \({N0|int}\) fish, the number is increasing at \({r|int}\) fish per year. Treating \(N\) as continuous, with \(\dfrac{dN}{dt}=kN\), find the value of \(k\).

A colony of cells has \(N\) cells at time \(t\) hours, and \(N\) increases at a rate proportional to \(N\). When \(N={N0|int}\), \(\dfrac{dN}{dt}={r|int}\). Find the constant of proportionality \(k\).

title: Doubling time for exponential growth
source: Theory P23-10.2 Quick check 2; e^(kt) = 2 gives t = ln 2 / k
stem: A quantity \(N\) satisfies \(\dfrac{dN}{dt}={k|raw}N\), where \(t\) is the time in years. Find the time taken for \(N\) to double.

steps.name: K
steps.note: Solve the equation, then set N = 2N0.

steps.name: A
steps.note: Take logarithms.

contexts.note: Includes the original dN/dt = 0.05N, doubling time 13.9 years

contexts.stem: An amount of money \(N\) grows so that \(\dfrac{dN}{dt}={k|raw}N\), with \(t\) in years. Find how long it takes for the amount to double.

contexts.stem: A tank holds \({a|int}\) litres when full. Water flows in so that the volume \(x\) litres at time \(t\) minutes satisfies \(\dfrac{dx}{dt}={k|raw}({a|int}-x)\). The tank is empty when \(t=0\). Find \(x\) when \(t={T|int}\).
The score \(x\) of a learner on a skill test after \(t\) days of practice satisfies \(\dfrac{dx}{dt}={k|raw}({a|int}-x)\), and \(x=0\) when \(t=0\). Find the score when \(t={T|int}\).

title: A decreasing insect population

source.note: Stem verbatim from the official QP; marks from the official MS. Question number checked against the QP.

stem:
The number of insects in a population \(t\) weeks after the start of observations is denoted by \(N\). The population is decreasing at a rate proportional to \(N\mathrm{e}^{-0.02t}\). The variables \(N\) and \(t\) are treated as continuous, and it is given that when \(t=0\), \(N=1000\) and \(\dfrac{dN}{dt}=-10\).

(i) Show that \(N\) and \(t\) satisfy the differential equation

\(\displaystyle\frac{dN}{dt}=-0.01\mathrm{e}^{-0.02t}N.\) [1]

(ii) Solve the differential equation and find the value of \(t\) when \(N=800\). [6]

(iii) State what happens to the value of \(N\) as \(t\) becomes large. [1]

steps.name: s1
steps.note: Official MS: B1 OE, state dN/dt = ke^(−0.02t)N and show k = −0.01 (−10 = k × 1 × 1000).

steps.name: s2
steps.note: Official MS: B1, separate variables correctly and integrate at least one side.

steps.name: s3
steps.note: Official MS: B1 OE, obtain term ln N.

steps.name: s4
steps.note: Official MS: B1 OE, obtain term 0.5e^(−0.02t).

steps.name: s5
steps.note: Official MS: M1, use N = 1000, t = 0 to evaluate a constant, or as limits, in a solution with terms a ln N and be^(−0.02t), where ab ≠ 0.

steps.name: s6
steps.note: Official MS: A1, obtain correct solution in any form, e.g. ln N − ln 1000 = 0.5(e^(−0.02t) − 1).

steps.name: s7
steps.note: Official MS: A1, substitute N = 800 and obtain t = 29.6.

steps.name: s8
steps.note: Official MS: B1, state that N approaches 1000/√e; accept 606 or 607 or 606.5.

title: Setting up a differential equation for a curve

source.note: Stem verbatim from the official QP; marks from the official MS. Question number checked against the QP.

stem:
A curve is such that the gradient at a general point with coordinates \((x, y)\) is proportional to \(\dfrac{y}{\sqrt{x+1} }\). The curve passes through the points with coordinates \((0, 1)\) and \((3, \mathrm{e})\).

By setting up and solving a differential equation, find the equation of the curve, expressing \(y\) in terms of \(x\). [7]

steps.name: s1
steps.note: Official MS: B1 OE, state equation dy/dx = ky/√(x + 1); must be a differential equation.

steps.name: s2
steps.note: Official MS: *M1, separate variables correctly for their differential equation and integrate at least one side.

steps.name: s3
steps.note: Official MS: A1, obtain ln y; allow M1A1A1 if they have assumed k = 1 or are working with an incorrect value for k.

steps.name: s4
steps.note: Official MS: A1, obtain 2[k]√(x + 1).

steps.name: s5
steps.note: Official MS: DM1 (dependent on *M1), use (0, 1) and (3, e) in an expression containing ln y and √(x + 1) and a constant of integration to determine k and/or c; stored as M1.

steps.name: s6
steps.note: Official MS: A1 OE, obtain k = ½ and c = −1 (ln y = √(x + 1) − 1); c depends on where it is placed in their equation.

steps.name: s7
steps.note: Official MS: A1 NFWW, OE, ISW, obtain y = exp(√(x + 1) − 1).
